hints.title: Digit Extraction and Count
hints.text: Determine the number of digits k in the integer n, then extract each individual digit.

hints.title: Power Sum Accumulation
hints.text: Raise each digit to the power k and compute the running sum.

hints.title: Equivalence Test
hints.text: Compare the accumulated sum to the original integer n and return whether they are identical.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def isArmstrong(self, n: int) -> bool:
        s = str(n)
        k = len(s)
        return sum(int(c) ** k for c in s) == n
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: There are no edge cases beyond digit extraction and modular arithmetic.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluating digits directly takes O(log10(N)) time and constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle digit separation cleanly without integer overflow.
complexity.notes: An Armstrong number equals the sum of its digits each raised to the power of the total number of digits.
